REGULAR EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
  MINUTES
  August 23, 2021

A regular meeting of the Equestrian Committee of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was
called to order by CHAIR HUFF at 7:08 P.M. via teleconference, pursuant to the
Governor’s Executive Order N-29-20.

Committee Members Present:  Huff, Silvano, Shinn, Ciarolla, Robinson, Griggs,
  Harik, Nilsen

Committee Members Absent:  Brtis, Martin, Zigrang

City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager, Alexa Davis
  Maintenance Superintendent, Mike Goldsmith

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  MEMBER SHINN moved, seconded by MEMBER ROBINSON, to:

  APPROVE THE DRAFT MINUTES OF THE JUNE 28, 2021 EQUESTRIAN
  COMMITTEE MEETING AS PRESENTED.

There being no objection, CHAIR HUFF so ordered.

AUDIENCE ITEMS WRITTEN /ORAL COMMUNICATIONS NOT ON AGENDA

None.

STAFF ITEMS

A. COVID-19 UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  Assistant City Manager (ACM) Davis provided an overview of the current status of
  COVID-19 restrictions. Currently, there are no changes to outdoor activities, nor
  equestrian related events or activities.

  CHAIR HUFF asked if the Governor extended the option to continue virtual
  meetings past September. ACM Davis responded that she was unaware if an
  extension was in effect at this time.

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
AUGUST 23, 2021
  1
 B. CITY CELEBRATION (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis provided an overview of the City Celebration planned for Saturday,
  September 25 from 9:00 A.M.- 3:00 P.M. with the poker ride starting at 8:00 A.M.;
  donations are actively being sought for prizes. She also shared equestrian events
  being planned, in coordination with PV Horsemen’s Association and the
  subcommittee of Equestrian Committee Members Ciarolla, Shinn, Martin and
  Silva. Committee Member Harik offered to assist as well.

C. EQUESTRIAN ISSUES LOG

  Maintenance Superintendent Goldsmith noted that two additional items were
  identified since the log was published last week: 1) a reported leaky valve at the
  Dapplegray Round Pen and 2) removal of loose subbase at Dapplegray Dressage
  Arena.

D. EQUESTRIAN EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis reported that City staff is working on the equestrian emergency
  preparedness that began in 2017. She explained that there had previously been a
  general horse count to determine how many horses are in the city and in what area
  they are concentrated to ultimately build supplies in those zones for emergency
  support. She further stated that staff is looking to re-establish the Equestrian
  Committee’s equestrian emergency subcommittee but some members have
  changed since the last meeting so staff is looking to reaffirm who will be involved.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER SHINN volunteered and stated the importance of the
  subcommittee. COMMITTEE MEMBER SILVA stated she would like to continue
  to participate as well. COMMITTEE MEMBERS ROBINSON and GRIGGS
  additionally volunteered to be part of the subcommittee as they represent different
  regions of the City.

  CHAIR HUFF asked when the peninsula-wide Emergency Expo was planned.
  ACM Davis responded that the event is scheduled on Sunday, October 24, 2021,
  tentatively from noon to 3:00 P.M., at Palos Verdes Peninsula High School as an
  outdoor event.

COMMITTEE REPORTS

A. ADOPT-A-TRAIL (VERBAL REPORT)

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
AUGUST 23, 2021
  2
   CHAIR HUFF inquired about the status of the trail business impacts and concerns
  from the Rolling Hills Estates neighbors that live adjacent to the PV Stables. ACM
  Davis provided an overview of the communications with the PV Stables, the trail
  operator and the City of Palos Verdes Estates. She explained that the trail
  operator now has his business license and permit. She also reported that it seems
  that most of the concerns are largely related to the activities happening on the
  Stables property which is within Palos Verdes Estates and that it appeared that
  the City was working with the Stables to address some issues. Further, ACM Davis
  stated that residents with direct concerns should directly speak with the Stables
  operator who was amenable to addressing issues, but that Palos Verdes Estates
  will be reviewing all their conditional use permits with the Planning Commission,
  including the Stables operation, which is an additional opportunity for the
  community to voice any remaining concerns. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith stated the Stables operator and trail business are open to suggestions,
  which he provided for trailers that come on site. COMMITTEE MEMBER GRIGGS
  shared that many of her neighbors are still impacted and report to her. CHAIR
  HUFF suggested the concerns be additionally forwarded to the City so staff is
  aware of any issues that remain. CHAIR HUFF additionally stated that the City
  will continue to work with the Stables and Palos Verdes Estates to ensure the
  issues are addressed.
  ACM Davis explained that the Committee assigned trails a couple years back but
  since have new members. Staff can plan on returning with the list of trails to
  review. COMMITTEE MEMBER HARIK stated that as equestrians they are on
  most trails and report anytime there is an issues. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith suggested this item be renamed “Trail Report.”

  COMMITTEE MEMBER GRIGGS stated that she is not assigned a trail as a new
  Committee Member but she lives near the Ferncreek trail and asked if there can
  be some asphalt chips added to the slope before it rains. Maintenance
  Superintendent Goldsmith responded that asphalt chips may not be available but
  they will add this area to their list for another possible solution.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER NILSEN stated that on a trail she identified as Ferncreek
  also, the clean-up of brush looked really good. Maintenance Superintendent
  Goldsmith stated that this particular area may be part of the former Fitzpatrick
  property which has recently changed ownership.

FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

A. PETER WEBER EQUESTRIAN CENTER CONTRACT RENEWAL

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
AUGUST 23, 2021
  3
   ACM Davis stated that staff would return with information on the Peter Weber
  Equestrian Center contract renewal as the contract ends in November. The item
  will be reviewed by the Equestrian Committee, Park and Activities Commission
  and approved by the City Council.

B. AMBASSADOR PROGRAM

  ACM Davis reported that once a new Community Services Supervisor is hired,
  staff will coordinate a subcommittee meeting and return to the Committee with
  more information.

CHAIR HUFF adjourned the Equestrian Committee meeting 7:40 P.M.

Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

__________________________  __________________________
Alexa Davis  Britt Huff, Chair
Assistant City Manager

EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE MEETING
AUGUST 23, 2021
  4
